This shamba is large, thirteen and a half hectares, and the soil here near the coast is sandy and gets tired quickly, so I will buy some urea to give the crops strength, though I cannot afford too much. I will also put manure from my animals because it helps the soil hold water better in this dry place. Because the plot is too big for me and my children to manage with hoes alone, I must hire laborers from the village to help with planting and weeding, but I will do much of the work myself. I will use the seeds I saved from last season and rely on the rains, as improved seeds for these crops are not easy to find here and spraying chemicals costs too much for a plot this size.
